summary.text: Genevieve Duchesneau is the Democratic candidate for the Vermont House of Representatives in the Rutland-8 District in the November 3, 2026 general election. A software engineer who lives in Proctor, she says she has never held office and is campaigning on property tax relief, health care costs and limits on surveillance technology.

paragraphs.text: Genevieve Duchesneau earned a high school diploma from Reno High School and a bachelor's degree from Post University in 2017, and her career experience includes working as a software engineer.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she has built software in machine learning, computer vision, autonomous-truck safety systems and health data systems for more than ten years, and co-founded the software startup Fixiv.
She said she served on the Rutland Pride board and volunteers with the Vermont Foodbank.
Duchesneau advanced from the Democratic primary on August 11, 2026.
In the survey she said she would push for income-based property tax relief and for lowering health care costs, and that she supports universal health care in Vermont.
She also said she opposes license plate cameras and large artificial intelligence data centers in Vermont.
